`sudo podman run -d --name homarr --user 1000:1000 -e 'PORT=7575' -p 7575:7575 -e 'SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY=82bf9755b947c26f59717f2d16e6630278262dc1805399a130162537ec074077' --mount type=bind,source=/home/namgo/homarr-mountpoint,destination=/appdata,bind-propagation=rslave ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:latest`

 to add some logs to the above error as encountered in my own configuration:

gives a 500 http error and in logs:
```
Error [TRPCClientError]: fetch failed
    at ta.from (.next/server/src/middleware.js:16:1640)

```

When a port is unspecified in the latest homarr container, it appears to default to `:3000`, is that correct?

When run with `-p 3000:3000` and no `PORT` environment variable specified, I am able to connect on `http://localhost:3000`. 7575/tcp doesn't appear to be in use in the container when running `podman exec [container] netstat `

In our current container we have the following ports allocated:
- **3000:** NextJS webapp (what you see)
- **3001:** Websocket server (Realtime updates)
- **6379:** Redis server (Realtime updates & Caching)
- **7575:** Nginx reverse proxy (To expose 3000 and 3001 under one port)

Thank you for the quick response! I believe I'm encountering two issues then and assumed they were the same.

I believe nginx reverse proxy is not launching, possibly because I've specified `--user`. I'll make a separate GH Issue for this specifically as it's definitely not related to the port number problem.

> In our current container we have the following ports allocated:
> 
> * **3000:** NextJS webapp (what you see)
> * **3001:** Websocket server (Realtime updates)
> * **6379:** Redis server (Realtime updates & Caching)
> * **7575:** Nginx reverse proxy (To expose 3000 and 3001 under one port)

Any way to map  -e 'PORT'='80' ?
Is it possible at all?
Thank you

> Thank you for the quick response! I believe I'm encountering two issues then and assumed they were the same.
> 
> I believe nginx reverse proxy is not launching, possibly because I've specified `--user`. I'll make a separate GH Issue for this specifically as it's definitely not related to the port number problem.

You can change the user with PUID and PGID, see https://homarr.dev/docs/advanced/running-as-different-user/

I've switched to using `PUID` and `PGID` environment variables in place of `--user` and now everything launches as normal.

I'll close the other GH Issue that I made as this addresses that. I understand `--user uid:gid` and `PUID/PGID` to be roughly equivalent so I'm not super concerned.

issue.title: bug: nginx appears to not launch under unprivileged docker

repository.name: homarr
repository.description: A modern and easy to use dashboard. 40+ integrations. 20K+ icons built in. Authentication out of the box. No YAML, drag and drop configuration.

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

docker with `--user` specified appears to cause nginx to not load correctly.

From logs:
```
run.sh: line 21: can't create /etc/nginx/nginx.conf: Permission denied
nginx: [alert] could not open error log file: open() "/var/lib/nginx/logs/error.log" failed (13: Permission denied)
2025/03/13 21:13:10 [warn] 13#13: the "user" directive makes sense only if the master process runs with super-user privileges, ignored in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:3
2025/03/13 21:13:10 [emerg] 13#13: mkdir() "/var/lib/nginx/tmp/client_body" failed (13: Permission denied)
```

### Steps to reproduce

`sudo podman run -d --name homarr --user 1000:1000 -p 3030:3000 -e 'SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY=82bf9755b947c26f59717f2d16e6630278262dc1805399a130162537ec074077' --mount type=bind,source=/home/namgo/homarr-mount,destination=/appdata,bind-propagation=rslave ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:latest`

### Impact

Users trying to run homarr unprivileged from a privileged docker daemon are not able to run the nginx reverse proxy. I believe this causes websockets to fail?

### Additional information

I'm aware that I'm using podman-run rather than docker-run, which might be unsupported but I am not exporting the container daemon socket to homarr, so I'm not sure if it makes a difference.

### Version

1.10.0

### Installation method

Docker Run

### Browser

Firefox

issue.title: feat: Support running as fully non-root containers

labels.name: decision
labels.description: A decision needs to be taken

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

repository.name: homarr
repository.description: A modern and easy to use dashboard. 40+ integrations. 20K+ icons built in. Authentication out of the box. No YAML, drag and drop configuration.

issue.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

I'd like to run homarr fully rootless inside the container by specifying the `user: 1234:1234` directive in the compose file. However, this isn't feasible because current `entrypoint.sh` chowns everything as the root user and then drop privileges via su-exec. The issue has been reported in #2154 and #2597.

To alleviate this, I've tried mounting an `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf` that follows some practices of [nginx-unprivileged](https://github.com/nginx/docker-nginx-unprivileged) like writing temp files to `/tmp`. I've also tried copying the `/app` repo to `/tmp` as the unprivileged user, and run the `run.sh` from there which worked. Details are as follow:

<details>
<summary>/etc/nginx/nginx.conf</summary>

```conf
events {
    worker_connections 1024;
}

# +++ err log and pid to /tmp
error_log  /tmp/error.log notice;
pid        /tmp/nginx.pid;

http {
    # +++ write temp files to /tmp
    proxy_temp_path /tmp/proxy_temp;
    client_body_temp_path /tmp/client_temp;
    fastcgi_temp_path /tmp/fastcgi_temp;
    uwsgi_temp_path /tmp/uwsgi_temp;
    scgi_temp_path /tmp/scgi_temp;

    server {
        listen 7575;

        # Route websockets traffic to port 3001
        # +++ hardcode hostnames
        location /websockets {
            proxy_pass http://homarr:3001;
            proxy_http_version 1.1;
            proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
            proxy_set_header Connection "Upgrade";
            proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
        }

        # Route all other traffic to port 3000
        location / {
            proxy_pass http://homarr:3000;
            proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $http_x_forwarded_proto;
            client_max_body_size 32M;
        }
    }
}

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>entrypoint.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -e
echo "Starting with UID='$PUID', GID='$PGID'"

cp -r /app /tmp
sh /tmp/app/run.sh
```
</details>


<details>
<summary>run.sh</summary>

```sh
# In line 4, add this command 
mkdir -p /tmp/logs

# ... other stuff ...

# add "-p /tmp" to the nginx command on line 26 or 27
# this will redirect logs to /tmp/logs/ as created above
nginx -g 'daemon off;' -p /tmp &
```

</details>

With this set up, I was able to spin up Homarr without using a root user on Podman, using this `podman-compose.yml` file:

```yaml
networks:
  test-network:
    external: true


services:
  homarr:
    container_name: homarr
    hostname: homarr
    image: ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - test-network

    # alternative entrypoint
    entrypoint: "/bin/sh"
    command: ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]
    ports:
      - '7575:7575'

    # mount the aforementioned volumes into /app
    volumes:
      - ./homarr/appdata:/appdata
      - ./homarr/entrypoint.sh:/app/entrypoint.sh:ro
      - ./homarr/run.sh:/app/run.sh:ro
      - ./homarr/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
    env_file:
       - ./homarr.env    

    # security options
    user: 1234:1234
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      no-new-privileges: true
```

Insofar, I've been able to connect to my reverse proxy and set up OpenID Connect, and create a dashboard that persists on reboot. So I think it works. The only error log I see from this approach is that some cache actions are still expecting the original path, but I don't think it has a breaking effect overall

```
 ⨯ Failed to write image to cache LHuqnU3UxZpbO5f-Ux2znSfOhD2tmibMIt8ytqnjPAs [Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/app/apps/nextjs/.next/cache'] {
  errno: -13,
  code: 'EACCES',
  syscall: 'mkdir',
  path: '/app/apps/nextjs/.next/cache'
}
```

---

As this proof-of-concept seems feasible, I'd like to kindly request rootless, unprivileged container to be supported. The app and itself is already runnable as non-root, the only difference is that instead of chowning its path, I'm copy-pasting it to some other place. The demo should show that this hackaround (or any other alternative way to implement rootless) shouldn't be too difficult to implement, given it's just switching around a few stuff from the entrypoints.

Would this be a viable option to run Homarr? I hope there can be a full solution which helps increase the security of my containers. Thanks in advance

### Additional information

Disclaimer: I'm not a professional, just a hobbyist, proceed with above approach at your own risk

issue.title: bug: wrong default port 7575 vs 3000
issue.body:
### Chart Version

8.16.1

### Bug Description

The default port in `values.yaml` is set to 7575, but the homarr image is actually exposing port 3000, the NextJS default port.
So with the default values in this chart, the ready-/livenessProbe and the connection to the UI fails.
The log showing port 3002 did also not not help debugging this:

Related: https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/issues/2154

PR follows

### values.yaml

```yaml
apiVersion: helm.cattle.io/v1
kind: HelmChart
metadata:
  name: homarr
  namespace: kube-system
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: homarr
spec:
  repo: https://homarr-labs.github.io/charts/
  chart: homarr
  targetNamespace: homarr
  valuesContent: |-
    image:
      repository: ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr
      pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      tag: "latest"

    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      # runAsUser: ...
      # runAsGroup: ...

    persistence:
      homarrDatabase:
        enabled: true
        storageClassName: "shared-folder"
        size: "50Mi"

    envSecrets:
      dbEncryption:
        existingSecret: "db-encryption"
        key: "db-encryption-key"

    containerPorts:
      http:
        port: 7575
        protocol: TCP

    service:
        enabled: true
        type: ClusterIP
        ports:
          app:
            port: 7575
            targetPort: http
            protocol: TCP

    livenessProbe:
      failureThreshold: 3
      initialDelaySeconds: 20
      timeoutSeconds: 1
      periodSeconds: 20
      httpGet:
        path: /api/health/live
        port: 7575

    readinessProbe:
      failureThreshold: 3
      initialDelaySeconds: 20
      timeoutSeconds: 1
      periodSeconds: 20
      httpGet:
        path: /api/health/ready
        port: 7575
```

### Relevant log output

```shell
# homarr pod log:
Tasks web server started successfully module="tasksMain" port="3002"

# Kubernetes Event:
Readiness probe failed: Get "http://<pi>:7575/api/health/ready": dial tcp <ip>:7575: connect: connection refused
```
